title: cohorted-flashfusion-kernel-scheduling-sketch
content:
Context:
We need a low-latency scheduling layer that lets fused FlashAttention kernels operate efficiently with paged KV caches under high concurrency. Existing approaches either over-serialize (kill throughput) or allow token storms to thrash paged KV and GPU memory. This doc sketches a cohort-based scheduler + kernel fusion framing that is aimed at: predictable 99th percentile latency, graceful backpressure when host<->device bandwidth is saturated, and high utilization for small to medium sequence lengths (8-1024).

Problem statement (short):
- Many incoming requests with diverse seq-lens cause interleaved kernel launches that fragment device occupancy and cause KV page thrash.
- Prefetch windows either fetch too much (waste memory) or too little (stall).
- FlashAttention fused ops need aligned work-chunks to enable tile-level shared-memory fusion; scattered single-token launches are inefficient.

High level idea: cohorted epochs + adaptive fusion boundary
- Group incoming requests into short-lived cohorts (epochs) by arrival time and by quantized sequence-length buckets.
- Within an epoch, the scheduler attempts kernel fusion across cohort members so that a single fused kernel handles multiple requests with similar sequence profiles.
- Epoch duration is bounded (e.g., 0.5ms - 5ms) to avoid user-visible batching delay; variable by latency SLO and traffic pattern.
- Introduce a fusion boundary concept: minimal contiguous token window per request that must be available in device memory before fusion proceeds. Fusion boundary is adaptive based on recent eviction/prefetch hit rate.

Key primitives and API surface (sketch for runtime infra):
- schedule_epoch(epoch_id, cohort_descriptor): returns a plan where tasks reference: model_variant, seq_bucket, kv_page_ranges, target_kernel_variant.
- request_hint(req_id, upstream): request gives hint: expected continuation length, user SLO, priority tag (system/user), cold_kv_pages boolean.
- prefetch_ticket(kv_page_ranges, ticket_id): low-overhead ticket used to orchestrate DMA prefetches and to attach backpressure counters.
- kernel_launch_plan: describes fused work segments and per-warp lane assignment; includes fallback paths when pages missing.

Memory and KV prefetch model:
- KV pages are prefetched on a per-cohort basis. Cohort prefetch orders pages by (hotness_score * cohort_overlap) / dma_cost.
- Staged prefetch: prioritize prefix pages (first N tokens across cohort) and then extend greedily until memory watermark reached.
- Watermarks: device_reserved (hard cap), device_soft (start eviction hints), host_prefetch_window (max outstanding DMA). Values are dynamically tuned by autoscaler telemetry.
- Opportunistic KV delta caching: detect cohort members with identical prefix hashes; share single page copy and remap lane pointers in kernel. This is cheap pointer shuffling rather than duplicate memcpy.

Backpressure and graceful degradation:
- Prefetch tickets carry a token budget. If DMA queue approaches host_prefetch_window, the scheduler either: (1) shrink epoch duration, (2) shrink fusion boundary to only operate on already present pages, or (3) reroute lower-priority requests to lighter-weight kernel variant (non-fused FlashAttn with streaming KV).
- Soft-fallback kernels: lower-latency but lower-throughput kernels that operate with partial KV on device (streaming mode). Useful to keep 99p bounded under memory contention.

Kernel fusion heuristics (device-side considerations):
- Fusion granularity is per-tile-group: attempt to pack sequences so that global tile occupancy is >= 70% for SMs assigned. If cohort cannot meet this occupancy within epoch timeout, fuse what is available but escalate to microbatch microkernel mode to avoid long blocking.
- Warp-lane sentinel: reserve 1-2 sentinel lanes per block for cooperative prefetch/eviction signaling (low-overhead consensus when a page is missing). This avoids heavy host round-trips for transient misses.
- Kernel should expose fast path for the common case (all pages present) and a slow path that coordinates device-level page pulls using NVLink peer copies or async DMA device API if supported.

Launch coordination and ordering:
- Epoch coordinator lives on host scheduler thread pool; launches kernels with a compact launch descriptor. Launches include a small ringbuf header so the kernel can claim work without atomics heavy usage across blocks.
- Use occupancy-guided launch parameters (threads/block, warps per request) determined by a per-model kernel profile. Profile is small JSON mapping seq_bucket->launch_params.

Instrumentation and signals (what to measure):
- per-epoch: cohort_size, avg_seq_len, fusion_rate, pages_prefetched, prefetch_hit_rate, dma_backlog_ms, epoch_wait_ms.
- per-kernel: SM_util, shared_mem_usage, slow_path_rate, sentinel_wakeups, per-request latency breakdown.
- alerts: prefetch_hit_rate < 80% for 1 minute => reduce fusion boundary; dma_backlog_ms > 10ms => tighten tickets.

Microbench plan (initial experiments):
1) Baseline: single-request FlashAttn fused kernel (current prod). Measure 95/99 latency under poisson arrival (lambda varied), seq-len mix [16,64,256].
2) Cohorted epoch with fixed 1ms window + fusion boundary = full-prefix. Measure throughput and 99p.
3) Adaptive boundary enabled (dynamic based on hit rate) vs fixed boundary.
4) Sentinel-lane coordinated device pulls vs host-driven DMA.

Metrics to collect: p50/p95/p99 latency per traffic pattern, device memory occupancy, per-page churn (evictions/sec), DMA throughput.

Open questions / TODOs:
- How to set default epoch duration per model? heuristics: inverse of 99p target (higher SLO -> shorter epoch) + traffic burstiness indicator. Need small experiment.
- Integration with existing paged-KV eviction: we rely on eviction hints from scheduler but eviction is currently a global LRU; we should add cohort-aware bias.
- Can we implement opportunistic device-to-device remapping of page pointers safely across CUDA versions? explore using virtual addressing APIs or memcpy bookkeeping.
- Fallback kernel design: what's the minimal implementation that keeps correctness but reduces memory pressure? Prototype in C++/CUDA.

Notes to self / rough action items:
- Prototype host-side epoch coordinator in runtime/scheduler/epoch_cohort.cc (sketch API above).
- Add small kernel stub that accepts fused descriptor + sentinel lane protocol. Start with microkernel that prints counters to ringbuf for validation.
- Perf harness: extend existing workload generator to emit cohort-aware arrival patterns and to simulate KV coldness.

References / prior art:
- FlashAttention v2 papers and tiling strategies (see repo notes).
- Internal: paged-kv eviction experiments (refer to JIRA-ENG-1420).
- NVidia async copy + CUDA clusters docs for device-to-device strategies.

Summary (one-liner):
Cohorted epochs + adaptive fusion boundaries aim to preserve low 99p latency while enabling efficient fused FlashAttention kernels with paged KV — via bounded batching, device-side sentinel coordination, and adaptive prefetch/backpressure tickets.
